bc_after_party.blurb: A riverside sport wall on the Cheekye River, north of Squamish in the Sea to Sky corridor, paired with its neighbour After Work. It holds eleven bolted lines, roughly twenty metres each, running from a single 5.9 and a couple of 5.10s up into a cluster of 5.11s, so it suits climbers who already lead the grade. The wall is vertical to a touch overhanging, with jugs, edges and small crimps, and the belays sit right above the water, giving it an exposed, multi-pitch feel. It faces south and picks up strong sun, though the right side leans east and cools off in the afternoon.

bc_predator.blurb: A single prominent boulder in the Predator Ridge zone above Arrow Lake in the West Kootenays, among the best-known blocks in the Castlegar-area bouldering. It carries eleven problems on clean gneiss, from a very easy start through to a handful at V5, with most of the line-up sitting in the V2 to V5 range. The face is slightly overhanging, and the climbing is regarded as some of the most distinctive face work at Arrow Lake: technical, sustained and not especially pumpy. The ridge setting gives broad views down to the lake from the top-outs, and the block works well as a first stop for a mid-grade session.

bc_reggae_wall.blurb: A steep limestone sport wall beside Slesse Creek in the Chilliwack River valley of the Fraser Valley. It has eleven bolted routes, all single pitch, ranging from a pair of 5.10s through a solid block of 5.11s to a few 5.12s, so it is aimed at strong sport leaders rather than beginners. The rock is tall, overhanging and of very good quality, with pockets and side pulls on the steeper sections, and loose fragments are possible so belayers do well to wear a helmet. It sits a short walk along a trail beyond the Middle Wall, in a quiet forested setting.

bc_a_the_euphorium.blurb: A small, overhung and stepped sport crag in the Northeastern Crags of Skaha Bluffs, near Penticton in the Okanagan. All eleven routes are bolted, and nearly all are 5.11, with four reaching 5.12, so it rewards climbers already comfortable on harder, moderately steep lines. The rock is featured, giving positive holds on the overhanging sections. It catches the early morning sun, which makes it a pleasant option for a cool start, and it is far enough from the busy central crags to feel like a quiet spot to spend the day.
